passage: The school canteen was so loud that everyone shouted. New boy Eshaan sat down next to Chinmay, who said, with a perfectly straight face, “I trained my pet elephant to do my homework, but he ate the notebook.” Chinmay's old friends laughed. Eshaan leaned in. “Really?” Chinmay held the flat face a second longer, then one eyebrow twitched. “No. I don't have an elephant.” Eshaan laughed with relief. Chinmay said, “Sorry. I should smile when I do that, so people know.” He tried a tiny smile, and it looked funny too.

qa.q: What did Chinmay say the elephant ate?
qa.a: He said the elephant ate the notebook.

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling when he said “Really?”, and what else could it have been?
qa.a: Confused and unsure, since the noisy canteen and Chinmay's flat face gave no clear sign it was a joke. He might also have been trying to be polite to someone he had just met.

qa.q: What small signal could help Chinmay make his jokes clearer?
qa.a: A twinkle in the eyes or a tiny smile, as he says he should do, so newcomers can tell it is a joke.

qa.q: How might Chinmay's old friends see the same joke?
qa.a: They know his style, so the flat face is part of what makes it funny for them.

grounding: A deadpan joke is funnier to those who know the style and confusing to others; a small signal helps.

passage:
“Nilesh, your homework?” said Mr Menon, holding out his hand.
“The dog ate it,” said Nilesh, without any expression. “He said it was hard to digest.”
Mr Menon's eyebrows rose. Several children giggled and Gurleen snorted. Nilesh took the notebook from his bag, the corner of his mouth twitching. “Here.”
Mr Menon studied him. “You have a very good straight face. Next time give me a smile as well, so I know.”
“Yes, sir,” said Nilesh. His eyes were bright.

qa.q: Who snorted when Nilesh said the dog ate his homework?
What was Mr Menon probably feeling when Nilesh said the dog ate it, and what else could it be?
qa.a: Probably puzzled or doubtful for a moment, since there was no sign it was a joke. His comment about a good straight face suggests he then saw the humour.

qa.q: What small signal could Nilesh add next time?
qa.a: A smile or a twinkle in his eyes, as Mr Menon asks, so people who do not know his style can tell it is a joke.

qa.q: How might Gurleen see Nilesh's joke differently from Mr Menon?
qa.a: She seems to know his style, so the flat face makes it funnier for her, while the teacher has to work out whether it is real.

grounding: A deadpan joke is funny to those who know the style and confusing to others.
